## Summary

Independent endorsement of the skill Thariq (@trq212) announced for the Claude Code team (see [[2026-10-06-trq212-html-plans-token-efficiency]]): it "turns Claude's plans into a page you click through and make decisions on" — which Kiss judges "way better than looking at a wall of Markdown": phone-friendly, and good at "distilling technical jargon into action." Ends with an install line (`claude https://t.co/...`) whose short link resolves to the tweet's own photo page, not a repo — the skill itself must be reached via Thariq's announcement thread.

## Why it matters

- **New claim in the thread: the review-side experience.** Thariq's own posts argued generation quality and token economics; this adds the consumer angle — plans as *interactive decision pages* (click through, decide) rather than a static document to re-read. That's a workflow claim, not a representation claim, and it's the first independent (non-author) signal on the skill.
- **Phone-friendly is the relevant axis for us.** The user reviews CoS artifacts (plans, briefs, receipts) mostly on their phone via WhatsApp/Telegram relays. A click-through decision format maps directly onto that review flow — the queued A/B experiment (Inbox task of 2026-10-01, nicopreme) should score phone readability and decision-throughput, not just review speed and error-finding.
- **Pattern echo:** same encode-once/standardize-the-artifact bet as [[2026-10-01-nicopreme-visual-explainer-skill]] and [[2026-10-06-trq212-html-plans-token-efficiency]] — third data point that plan-as-HTML-page is becoming a convention among agent-tool builders, not a one-off.
- **Skepticism gates:** endorsement predates broad availability (skill described as pre-release on Oct 5); "way better" is one power user's impression with no artifact shown beyond screenshots we couldn't analyze; the install link is unresolvable at capture, so the exact tool evaluated can't be confirmed.
